scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported 1492 to 1500 polygon is unchanged and unverified. Archaeological site dating, mission chronology and community identity are distinct.
The 1982 report revises the longer 1980 report. Both are one underlying research project; only the inspected 1982 pages are cited. Pages 2, 3, 10 to 15 and figures were visually inspected.

Site 41CH22 is a proposed Orcoquisac camp, not an established ethnic attribution. Its blue bead was a surface find in a pipeline corridor. At 41CH57, later colonial occupation overlies a prehistoric shell midden.

The contemporary interview broadly describes Atakapa agriculture, while the 1982 study describes Orcoquisac fishing, hunting and gathering without agriculture. The card does not universalize either subsistence account.
Texas Beyond History says abandonment in 1771; the 1982 report describes remaining personnel departing early in 1772. The phase is explicitly approximate and gives both years.
No equation of Han, Coaque or Caux with Akokisa is asserted; Campbell presents those as proposed identifications.
Mary Leblanc’s testimony supports living identity and continuity. Unverified mound dimensions, environmental absolutes and a mistaken 1820s Texas independence chronology are not repeated.
The former community website currently contains unrelated pharmaceutical spam and is not used as a source. The independently hosted interview is the direct community testimony cited.
Independent historical review and geometry assessment remain pending.
